source_text:
ἀποστόλοις εἰπών· Λάβετε, φάγετε, τοῦτό ἐστι τὸ σῶμά μου τὸ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν κλώμενον εἰς
ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν. Ὡσαύτως μετὰ τὸ δειπνῆσαι, λαβὼν ποτήριον καὶ κεράσας ἐκ δύο
στοιχείων, ἐκ γεννήματος ἀμπέλου καὶ ὕδατος, ἐσφράγισε ποτήριον ἀθανασίας καὶ
ἔδωκε τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ εἰπών· Πίετε ἐξ αὐτοῦ πάντες, τοῦτό ἐστι τὸ αἷμά μου τὸ τῆς
καινῆς διαθήκης τὸ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν καὶ πολλῶν ἐκχυνόμενον εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν».
thought_title: The Words of Institution for Bread and Cup
orientation: Christ, having blessed the bread, now speaks the words of institution to his apostles and then likewise blesses and gives the cup.
pass_a_gloss: Christ said to the apostles: Take, eat, this is my body, the one for you broken for forgiveness of sins. Likewise after the supper, having taken a cup and having mixed from two substances, from fruit of the vine and water, he consecrated the cup of immortality and gave it to his disciples, saying: Drink from it, all of you, this is my blood, the one of the new covenant, the one for you and for many poured out for forgiveness of sins.

choices.why: The source uses ἀποστόλοις here, not μαθηταῖς, so the literal rendering preserves the distinction from the disciples mentioned later in the same sentence.
The participle κεράσας means having mixed, and στοιχείων is rendered as elements to keep the literal sense of constituent parts, matching the liturgical language of the source.
The verb σφραγίζω literally means to seal, and the source uses it here rather than a verb of blessing or sanctifying, so the literal rendering preserves the specific action.
The glossary fixes this rendering, and the literal genitive ἀθανασίας is preserved as of immortality.

choices.english: the one of the new covenant
choices.why: The article τὸ with the genitive is rendered as the one of to keep the literal appositional structure, and καινῆς διαθήκης follows the glossary as new covenant.
The present passive participle ἐκχυνόμενον is rendered literally as being poured out, preserving the continuous or ritual sense of the shedding.

pass_b_english: to the apostles, saying, “Take, eat; this is my body, which is being broken for you for the forgiveness of sins.” In the same way, after supper, he took the cup, having mixed it from two elements—from the fruit of the vine and water—sealed the cup of immortality, and gave it to his disciples, saying, “Drink from it, all of you; this is my blood of the new covenant, which is being poured out for you and for many for the forgiveness of sins.”

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'cup of immortality' but 'sealed' is not the fixed term; however, ἐσφράγισε means 'sealed/signed', not in glossary. The real issue: 'sealed the cup of immortality' uses 'sealed' which is not glossary-fixed, but more critically the glossary term is 'cup of immortality'—this is used correctly. Wait: checking again—'sealed' is translation of ἐσφράγισε, not a glossary term. No glossary violation. But checking 'cup of immortality'—yes, matches glossary. Re-checking: actually no glossary error. Let me re-verify... The glossary says 'ποτήριον ἀθανασίας' = 'cup of immortality'. English has 'cup of immortality'—correct. No finding.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐσφράγισε means 'sealed'; ποτήριον ἀθανασίας correctly rendered 'cup of immortality'. No glossary violation.
